 Print ' Hanuman Ansh', starring Shobhinaw Satyaa, is preparing to make its digital debut after an impressive theatrical run. The devotional drama reportedly earned more than Rs 450 crore worldwide despite being made on a budget of around Rs 2 crore. Its unexpected commercial success made it one of the notable box-office stories of 2026. Now, viewers who missed its theatrical release will have an opportunity to watch the film online. The movie draws inspiration from the life and teachings of Neem Karoli Baba, the renowned spiritual guru. Rather than focusing only on religious events, the narrative explores personal grief, faith and the importance of compassion. Its central character's search for spiritual understanding forms the emotional foundation of the story. 'Hanuman Ansh' OTT release date and streaming platform
 According to the official announcement, 'Hanuman Ansh' will premiere on SonyLIV on November 27, 2026. The film's arrival on the streaming platform follows its successful run in theatres. What is the story of 'Hanuman Ansh'?
 Shobhinaw Satyaa plays the lead role in the film, which takes audiences through a spiritual journey inspired by Neem Karoli Baba. The movie combines elements of devotion and human emotion to explore the influence of faith on everyday life. The narrative centres on Lakshman Das, a young boy whose life changes following his mother's death. Struggling with the loss, he begins searching for God and trying to understand the meaning of life. His personal journey gradually leads him towards Neem Karoli Baba. Neem Karoli Baba's teachings form the film's central theme
 One of the movie's key ideas is that spirituality extends beyond miracles and extraordinary experiences. The narrative places importance on simple acts of kindness and service. Feeding hungry people, helping those facing difficulties and supporting others without expecting anything in return are presented as meaningful expressions of faith. What did ETimes say about 'Hanuman Ansh'?
 ETimes' review described the movie as a reflective exploration of grief, belief and humanity. It also observed that the film's slow, contemplative storytelling might not appeal to audiences looking for conventional dramatic highs. However, viewers who connect with its approach may appreciate the message it conveys. ETimes review for the film read, "Hanuman Ansh is ultimately less a conventional biopic than a spiritual reflection on grief, faith and service. It won't work equally well for viewers looking for pace or conventional dramatic highs, but those willing to settle into its contemplative rhythm will find a film that leaves behind a simple, humane message: love, serve and have faith."
